provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Names a bounded stretch of time, one with a clear start and end, throughout which the main clause holds (雨が降っている間は待とう). 間に instead places a one-off event somewhere inside that stretch; among the siblings, うちは adds that the span will end and 限りは states a condition rather than a period. It attaches to plain verbs and i-adjectives, to な-adjectives with な (静かな間は), and to noun+の (雨の間は).

examples.ruby: 雨[あめ]が降[ふ]っている間[あいだ]は、店[みせ]の中[なか]で待[ま]とう。
examples.english: Let's wait inside the shop for as long as it keeps raining.

examples.ruby: 子[こ]どもが昼寝[ひるね]をしている間[あいだ]は、テレビを消[け]しておく。
examples.english: I keep the TV off the whole time the kids are napping.

examples.ruby: 信号[しんごう]が赤[あか]い間[あいだ]は、絶対[ぜったい]に渡[わた]らない。
examples.english: As long as the light is red, you don't cross — ever.

glosses: while (it still is); as long as it lasts
patterns.usage_note: Frames the span as a state that will not last, so the main clause is what holds, or what to do, before the change arrives (若いうちは無茶ができる). 間は names the same stretch neutrally, with no suggestion of change, and 限りは sets a condition instead of a period. It takes な-adjectives with な and nouns with の (元気なうちは, 独身のうちは), and collocates with states that fade: 若い, 明るい, 元気, 〜ている.

examples.ruby: 若[わか]いうちは、少[すこ]しくらい無茶[むちゃ]をしてもいい。
examples.english: While you're still young, you can afford to overdo it a little.

examples.ruby: 母[はは]が起[お]きているうちは、台所[だいどころ]の電気[でんき]は消[け]せない。
examples.english: I can't turn the kitchen light off while my mother is still up.

examples.ruby: 日[ひ]が高[たか]いうちは、猫[ねこ]は縁側[えんがわ]から動[うご]こうとしない。
examples.english: While the sun is still high, the cat won't budge from the veranda.

glosses: as long as; so long as
patterns.usage_note: States a condition rather than a time span: the main clause holds only while that condition does, with the opposite implied once it stops (私が生きている限りは売らせない). 間は and うちは name periods; 限りは is more emphatic and more formal, and pairs with commitments and with statements of impossibility. Besides plain verbs it takes nouns and な-adjectives through である (学生である限りは), and in the common 〜ない限り "unless" は is usually dropped.

examples.ruby: この会社[かいしゃ]に籍[せき]を置[お]く限[かぎ]りは、規則[きそく]に従[したが]う。
examples.english: So long as my name is on this company's books, I'll follow its rules.

examples.ruby: 私[わたし]が生[い]きている限[かぎ]りは、この土地[とち]は売[う]らせない。
examples.english: As long as I'm alive, I won't let anyone sell this land.

examples.ruby: 選手[せんしゅ]が望[のぞ]む限[かぎ]りは、支援[しえん]を打[う]ち切[き]らない。
examples.english: Provided the athlete still wants it, we won't cut off support.
